title: diff-harness gates main on diagnostic text and has been red since 2026-11-16
description:
## The problem

.github/workflows/diff-harness.yml went red on main around 2026-11-16 and stayed red through at least three main pushes, including today's. Nobody looked. I did not know the workflow existed until I read gh run list after pushing 61 commits on top of it.

A gate that cries wolf stops being read, and then it is worse than no gate: it occupies the slot where a real signal would go.

## Why it is red, and why that is the gate's fault

Two causes, both third-party rather than pkix-path.

1. EIGHT CHAINS DRIFTED Agreement -> DiagnosticDivergence (71 -> 63 and 49 -> 58 against pkix-difftest/baseline-pkits.json).

   Class::DiagnosticDivergence means "everyone agrees on Pass/Fail but differs on the reason". So no verdict changed. pkix-path decided the same thing about every chain; only the oracles' error WORDING moved. Near-certainly an OpenSSL or pyca version bump on the runner.

   The harness already documents this exposure in its own workflow comment: "The diff harness's verdicts are sensitive to the exact OpenSSL build (option string parsing, error wording) and pyca release." The gate was built knowing it would drift, and then pinned the drift-prone values in a committed baseline anyway.

2. TWO HARNESS ERRORS, each an oracle limitation rather than a defect:
   - pyca on "4.1.5 Valid DSA Parameter Inheritance Test5" -- pyca's ASN.1 parser rejects an SPKI with inherited/absent DSA parameters.
   - pkix-path on "4.2.3 Valid pre2000 UTC notBefore Date Test3" -- der 0.8.3 cannot represent a pre-1970 UTCTime. See PKIX-str9; fail-closed, no security impact.

   Both surface as anonymous "harness error(s) during run; chains skipped from classification", so they look like breakage rather than known gaps.

## What to decide

The gate's job is catching pkix-path regressions. It currently also catches OpenSSL and pyca release notes. Options, roughly in order of how much they are worth:

- PIN THE ORACLE VERSIONS. Install a fixed OpenSSL and a pinned pyca/cryptography in the job rather than taking whatever ubuntu-latest ships. Makes the baseline meaningful; costs a periodic deliberate bump, which is the right place for that cost.
- COMPARE VERDICT CLASSES, NOT DIAGNOSTIC TEXT. Treat Agreement and DiagnosticDivergence as one bucket for gating purposes, since neither represents a verdict disagreement. Keeps the signal that matters (LooserThanWild, StricterThanWild, OracleDivergence) and drops the one that drifts. Cheapest real fix.
- MAKE KNOWN GAPS EXPLICIT. An expected-failure list, so 4.1.5 and 4.2.3 stop reading as errors and a NEW harness error is visible again.
- FAIL LOUDLY OR NOT AT ALL. If the gate stays drift-prone, it should not gate main. A scheduled run that opens an issue would be more honest than a red X everyone learns to scroll past.

## Also worth checking

Whether anything else regressed during the week the gate was red. The drift analysis above says verdicts did not change, which is reassuring, but it was derived from log lines rather than from a clean local run with pinned oracles. Worth one deliberate run to confirm before trusting it.

## Acceptance

[ ] Root cause of the 8-chain drift confirmed (oracle version bump, or something else)
[ ] Gate redesigned so a third-party version bump cannot make it red
[ ] 4.1.5 and 4.2.3 recorded as expected gaps rather than anonymous harness errors
[ ] diff-harness green on main, and a note on what it will and will not catch
